overview: SEIL Lab investigates how people attend to social information, integrate cues across senses, and interact and cooperate with humans and artificial agents. We connect cognitive experiments, neuroscience and computational modelling with human-robot and human-AI research. Across five complementary themes, artificial agents serve both as interaction partners and as experimental tools: helping us test accounts of human social behaviour and develop human-grounded embodied AI.
homeIntro: Our research connects crossmodal social cue integration and the mechanisms of social cognition with human-robot cooperation, human-AI interaction and embodied AI.
approachTitle: Human mechanisms, testable models and interactive agents
approach: Human experiments help us identify which social cues guide behaviour and distinguish competing explanations. Computational models turn these accounts into testable predictions; implementing selected models on robots lets us examine them under embodied conditions. We also manipulate robot and conversational-agent behaviour to investigate how people respond during interaction. Findings feed back into our questions and models. Different projects enter this cycle at different points, linking fundamental work on human cognition with studies of cooperation and interaction with AI.
piResearch: She investigates how social cues guide attention, how people integrate information across senses, and how they interact and cooperate with robots and AI systems. Her work connects cognitive experiments and computational modelling with studies of embodied robots, voice assistants and conversational agents, using artificial systems both to investigate human social mechanisms and to explore human-grounded AI.
